query: Which of these battles occurred earlier--the Battle of Peleliu or the Battle of Belleau Wood?

The Battle of Peleliu is believed to be one of the earliest and most significant battles in World War I, occurring on July 23, 1918. It was fought between the French and German forces at the village of Peleliu, near the town of Belleau Wood, in northern France. The battle took place during World War I, and it marked a turning point for the Allies in the war.

The Battle of Belleau Wood is believed to have occurred on July 26, 1918, when the Allied forces under the command of General John Pershing attacked the German lines at Belleau Wood, near the village of Belleau-Woods. The battle was a decisive victory for the Allies and ended the German offensive in France.

Both battles were fought on land, with both sides using trenches, machine guns, and artillery to devastating effect. The Battle of Peleliu saw the French army defeat the German forces at Peleliu, while the Battle of Belleau Wood saw the Allied forces capture the village of Belleau-Woods from the Germans.

Both battles were significant events in World War I, contributing to the Allied victory and paving the way for the Allied occupation of France.
